questions.stem: What does Data Value Realisation refer to?
options: The process of selling all company data to the highest bidder
The process of actualising the value inherent in data through strategies, practices or initiatives that achieve tangible benefits
The process of archiving data once it has no further use
The process of encrypting data to protect its value
The process of counting how many records a company holds
questions.explanation: Data Value Realisation is the process of actualising or realising the value inherent in data, through strategies and initiatives aimed at leveraging data for tangible outcomes.

questions.stem: What does Monetisation of Data mean within Data Value Realisation?
options: Charging employees for access to reports
Converting all data into a single currency field
Paying a vendor to store the data
Extracting economic value from data, for example through new revenue streams or cost savings
Printing data onto invoices
questions.explanation: Monetisation of data means extracting economic value from it, for instance by identifying new revenue streams or cost savings through data-driven initiatives.

questions.stem: Which example of Data Value Realisation uses sensor data to anticipate equipment failures?
options: Predictive Maintenance
Customer Experience improvement
Cost Optimisation
Data Monetisation
Strategy Alignment
questions.explanation: Predictive Maintenance uses sensor data analysis to anticipate equipment failures, reducing downtime and maintenance costs.

questions.stem: Which of these is NOT one of the five key levers for validating and unlocking the value of data?
options: Data volume
Data quality
Use cases
Usefulness of use cases
Storage cost
questions.explanation: The five key levers are data volume, data quality, use cases, usefulness of use cases, and how strategy is aligned with those use cases; storage cost is not among them.

questions.stem: Which intangible elements are said to play a crucial role in realising the value of data?
options: Server capacity, bandwidth and disk speed
Tax rates, interest rates and inflation
Leadership, cooperation, talent and culture
Encryption, backups and firewalls
Office space, furniture and lighting
questions.explanation: Beyond the tangible levers, intangible elements such as leadership, cooperation, talent and culture also play a crucial role.

questions.stem: What are the two main reasons given for calculating the value of data?
options: To determine its sale price, and to use it as a primary indicator of the performance of your data management
To satisfy auditors, and to set employee bonuses
To choose a cloud provider, and to size the storage budget
To decide what to delete, and to justify a new database
To price insurance, and to calculate depreciation
questions.explanation: The value of data is calculated to determine its sale price and to serve as a primary indicator of how well data management is performing.

questions.stem: How is the value of data calculated?
options: Data value = Market value plus Internal value
Data value = Internal value minus management cost
Data value = the average of Market value and Internal value
Data value = the maximum of its Market value and its Internal value
Data value = Market value divided by data volume
questions.explanation: The value of data is the maximum of its Market value and its Internal value: Data value = Max [Data Market Value, Data Internal Value].

questions.stem: What does it mean if your actions increase the value of your data by more than the cost of managing it?
options: The data should be sold immediately
You are on the right track with your data management
The data has become a liability
The market value must be recalculated
Data management costs should be cut
questions.explanation: If your actions increase the value of your data more than the cost of managing it, it means you are on the right track.

questions.stem: What is implied if the value your organisation gets from its data is NOT greater than what it would obtain by selling that data?
options: The data has no market value
The organisation should stop collecting data
The data must be encrypted
The data volume is too small
Either others can manage your data better than your company, or the synergies from using the data internally are not good enough
questions.explanation: Successful data management should make the data worth more than its sale price; if not, either others can manage it better or the internal synergies are insufficient.

questions.stem: What shift in thinking does Data Value Realisation call for regarding strategy?
options: Moving from a data strategy back to a business strategy
Moving from internal data to purchased data
Moving from using data for your strategy to having a specific data strategy with clear roles, objectives and an action plan
Moving from measuring data value to ignoring it
Moving from cloud storage to on-premises storage
questions.explanation: It is about moving from merely using data for your strategy to having a data strategy of its own, with clear roles and responsibilities, objectives and a detailed action plan.
